channel.title: The Batch | DeepLearning.AI
channel.description: Weekly AI news for engineers, executives, and enthusiasts.

item.title: A Single Decoder Turns Small Models into Action: TurboVLA turns to a throwback architecture to attend to language and vision
item.description: The vision-language-action architecture that increasingly drives robots relies on a large language model to combine visual observations with text instructions before an action decoder produces motor commands.

item.title: Nvidia Courts A New Partner: Reflection releases Beam, an open weight model from an independent U.S.-based lab
item.description: Reflection AI, a closely-watched, Nvidia-backed U.S. startup, announced its first model.

item.title: ChatGPT for Teens Gets a Report Card: OpenAI adds features for youths as studies doubt program's safety and educational impact
item.description: OpenAI announced that it would add college-planning and study tools to its under-18 experience.

item.title: Meta Releases Wonder, Opens Spark: All about Muse Wonder (API), Muse Wonder Full (subscription), and Muse Spark Open (weights available)
item.description: Meta marched all the way back to the AI frontier to offer a Muse model for everyone.

item.title: The Four Ps — A Leadership Framework: How to Manage An AI-Native Engineering Team
item.description: What should an engineering leader such as a VP Engineering or an Engineering manager do to help their team become more proficient in AI?

item.description: The Batch News & Insights: What should an engineering leader such as a VP Engineering or an Engineering manager do to help their team become more proficient in AI?

item.title: Minimax’s M3.1 Flash Cuts Prices: Critical PHP bug found by AI affects majority of web sites
item.description: Mercury 3, diffusion-based alternative to Claude Haiku. d1-ultra, a highly accurate decision model. Using OpenAI’s models to rewrite and repair legacy code. llm-d, an all-around optimizer for serving open models.

item.title: Muse Spark Open leads U.S. open models: Reflection releases weights for Beam, a much-anticipated model
item.description: Grok Voice 3.0 leads voice-to-voice benchmarks. Nvidia 3.5 Super VL is faster, more capable than Lightning. DeepSeek-V-4.1-Flash pushes strong update. Meta amends controversial Muse scraping terms.

item.title: Data Mixing, Minus the Guesswork: Research from the team behind CausalMix offers a technique to select fine-tuning examples
item.description: When you’re building a fine-tuning dataset, finding a mix of subject domains that yields a high-performing model can require expensive trial and error, because fine-tuned performance also depends on the quality of the individual examples.

item.title: Computers Built for Local AI: Apple’s Mac mini and Mac Studio have competition from Microsoft and Nvidia
item.description: Developers have warmed to the economics and security of local models, either as an alternative or a complement to the cloud.

item.title: Mistral’s Sovereign Appeal: Mistral Large 4, the leading European AI model, outperforms all open models outside of China
item.description: Mistral’s latest model is its largest and most capable, and the most powerful yet released by a European company.

item.title: Claude Fills Out Its Model Family: Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 give developers fast, highly capable alternatives to Opus 5.5
item.description: Claude Haiku, Anthropic’s fastest and least expensive model gets a long-awaited update.

item.title: Formal Verification Meets Unverifiable Judgement: Don’t Overgeneralize from Progress in Math and Code — The Hardest AI Problems Still Require More Work
item.description: The gulf between LLM performance on verifiable tasks vs. unverifiable tasks that require judgement is larger than most people realize.
